reading.body:
AI infrastructure companies are actively hiring for governance roles as compute and policy become entangled operational concerns.

The five open positions span model makers, deployment platforms, and enterprise software vendors. Cohere seeks a public policy manager focused explicitly on compute and infrastructure. Anthropic is hiring regulatory counsel. Databricks and ServiceNow are building internal governance capacity. The roles posted between April and September 2026 reflect companies embedding policy expertise alongside their technical stacks rather than outsourcing it.

This matters because scaling AI requires navigating compute allocation, data sovereignty, and infrastructure siting, all of which intersect with regulation. Companies cannot separate these from their core operations. A governance role at a model company is not a compliance afterthought. It shapes which markets they can access, how they source power and hardware, and what constraints they accept on data flows.

The data covers posted jobs only and reflects hiring signals at a single moment. It does not show whether these roles are new or replacement, how many applications arrived, or what compensation these positions command. It captures announced intent, not execution or market success.
